giris_tr: Türkiye'de yayılış gösteren türlerin güncel listesi; yazarlar, Türkçe adlar, endemizm ve IUCN kategorileriyle. Ayrıntıları ve fotoğrafları görmek için bir türe tıklayın.
kaynak_tr: Hazırlayan: Doç. Dr. Muammer Kurnaz · Son güncelleme: Ekim 2026
giris_en: An up-to-date checklist of the species occurring in Türkiye, with authors, Turkish names, endemism and IUCN categories. Select a species to see its details and photographs.
kaynak_en: Compiled by Assoc. Prof. Muammer Kurnaz · Last updated: October 2026

species.kaynak_notu: Split from P. syriacus (2019); ASW reports a hybrid zone with P. syriacus.
Pre-2019 Turkish literature may include P. balcanicus; hybrid zone extends into Türkiye.
ASW calls the 2021 genus Pelodytopsis arbitrary and keeps Pelodytes.

ASW (15 Pelophylax spp.) does not list P. bedriagae, P. caralitanus or P. kurtmuelleri as species; bedriagae and caralitana (type locality Beysehir Lake, Turkey) are in the synonymy of P. ridibundus. Anatolian water frogs are often treated as P. bedriagae / P. cf. bedriagae in Turkish literature. The Geographic Occurrence section could not be retrieved (page too long); presence in Türkiye inferred from the synonymy and comments.
ASW author/year is Fitzinger, 1838 (other sources cite Bonaparte, 1840).
ASW includes R. holtzi and R. camerani within R. macrocnemis (status of both discussed as debated).
Valid species in ASW, distinct from R. macrocnemis (Veith et al. 2003 and later studies).
ASW distribution reaches only European Turkey (Thrace).
ASW notes Anatolian 'B. b. spinosus' records are referable to B. bufo and/or B. verrucosissimus; hybrid zone with B. verrucosissimus in Rize. B. verrucosissimus is not in the input list.
ASW treats B. sitibundus as a subspecies of B. viridis (following Speybroeck et al. 2020); B. sitibundus and B. variabilis are not recognized species in ASW Bufotes (12 spp.).
Removed from H. arborea synonymy in 2008; older Turkish records under H. arborea. ASW mentions a hybrid zone with H. arborea in western Türkiye.
Southern populations from Yemen to Syria are H. felixarabica; Cyprus/Türkiye-Iran lineage keeps H. savignyi. Contact zone with H. orientalis.
ASW Lissotriton has 8 spp.; L. schmidtleri (the Turkish taxon) and L. lantzi are not counted as species (treated as subspecies of L. vulgaris).
Valid species in ASW: elevated from subspecies of L. luschani by Scott et al. (2024 "2025"). Turkish name missing in input. | IUCN: covered by the L. luschani assessment (EN, 2023)
Not endemic: ASW lists Greece (Kastellorizo Island) as well as Türkiye. Range Patara to Demre after finikensis split.

ASW genus Mertensiella currently has 1 sp.; M. djanaschvilii (resurrected by Raffaëlli 2022 for SW Georgia/NE Türkiye populations) is not counted, Tarkhnishvili et al. (2026) having rejected its species status. A separate M. djanaschvilii page still exists on ASW.
ASW lists N. barani and N. munzurensis as names within N. strauchii; Koster et al. (2025) rejected their species/subspecies status. ASW Neurergus has 4 spp.
IUCN: no separate assessment
ASW keeps semenovi and orientalis within S. infraimmaculata (species status of semenovi discussed as unclear).
Northern Anatolian populations now T. anatolicus.
In Türkiye restricted to the northeast (genetically confirmed from Posof, Ardahan); western Anatolian 'karelinii' are T. anatolicus x T. ivanbureschi hybrids, northern ones T. anatolicus.
